title: fix(objectql)!: a predicate update judges each matched row against the parent roll-ups the rows before it move
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9CEK3WVYUqxMjpD1xegmPGF)_

Fixes #34465

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — skills/** teaches the per-row hook semantics of a predicate (`multi: true`) write (skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md, lines 181 and 195) but says nothing on how a rule reads a parent summary during one

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：按条件批量更新（`update(..., { where, multi: true })`，flow 的 update_record 节点 `multi: true`）时，读父记录汇总的校验规则和明细字段的 `parent.` 条件，现在每一行读到的是「前面已判过的匹配行改完之后」的汇总，和逐条 by-id 更新的结果一致。count/sum/min/max/avg 都精确，换父也算；规则读的是父记录上建在汇总上的公式或存储计算字段（如 `remaining = budget - spent`）时，也按叠加后的汇总重算。
- 为什么改：裁决 6377847361（C，插入）和 6928862195（B，updateMany）已定「批量等于逐条」，谓词更新是剩下唯一不守它的批量门；席位在卡上按路线 A 裁定（6938087434）。
- 风险与回滚：收窄（BREAKING）：今天能整批写进去的某些谓词更新会被整批拒收（只影响有规则读父汇总的子对象，hotcrm 与示例应用里没找到）。也有反方向：前面的行把汇总往放行方向推时，main 会拒的更新现在会放行，和逐条一致。没有这类规则、或只匹配一行时，零额外开销。三种情形读存值（下面单列一节）。回滚即撤回本 PR，无数据迁移。
- 先看：`packages/objectql/src/summary-batch-accumulation.ts`（末尾新增 `loadPredicateUpdateSummaryBases` 与 `createPredicateUpdateSummaryFold`）、`packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts`（谓词分支校验循环）、`packages/objectql/src/summary-rollup.test.ts`（末尾 #34465 一组）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/summary-rollup.test.ts src/summary-batch-accumulation.test.ts`，预期全过；其中 #34465 共 22 条；去掉逐行推进（`advance`）后 5 条变红，去掉计算字段重算后 3 条变红。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地（Tier H，需契约档 L2 审核记录）。

## What changes

A predicate update judges every matched row before its one `updateMany`, against related rows (`resolvePredicateRelated`) and master-detail headers (`resolveMasterDetailParents`) read once for the batch, and recomputes the roll-ups once after it. So every row read a parent summary as it stood before the update. Measured on `main` before this change: with "one primary line per invoice" (`record.is_primary == true && record.inv.primaries > 0`), two by-id updates admit the first line and refuse the second, but one predicate update admits both and leaves `primaries` at 2.

- `packages/objectql/src/summary-batch-accumulation.ts`
  - `loadPredicateUpdateSummaryBases(engine, descriptors, matched, ctx)` reads, per summary a rule reads and per chunk of parents, one grouped aggregate (`groupBy` the FK, `ROLLUP_AGGREGATE_OPTION` on the FK, a system context like the recompute). The parents are those the matched rows name, as stored or as the update leaves them.
    - `count` / `sum` / `avg`: every child as stored, the matched rows included. `avg` reads its sum and non-null count.
    - `min` / `max`: the children outside the matched set (`id $nin`), since an extreme cannot be taken back out.
  - `createPredicateUpdateSummaryFold(bases, matched, childFields)` folds the matched rows in memory. Before row k, rows 0..k-1 have left their stored contribution and taken the one the update gives them. It exposes `overlay(binding)` and `overlayRow(object, header)`, the same two shapes as the insert arm, plus `advance(i)`. The summary `filter` is evaluated on each row state by the in-memory aggregation's own walker.
  - The fold also patches the parent's fields that are calculated from a folded roll-up: a `formula`, or a stored computed field (an `expression` on a field that is not a formula), directly or through another such field. A rule can read one of these instead of the roll-up (`record.project.remaining`, where `remaining = budget - spent`). `setDependents` hands the fold what computes them, and `foldedSummaries()` says which roll-ups and parents it moves.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts` — in the predicate branch's per-row validation loop, when a rule reads a summary of this object and more than one row matched, it builds the fold. It then judges row i against the overlaid related binding and header (and the previous header), and advances. `loadSummaryFoldDependents` handles the calculated fields the way a by-id update's rule reads the parent, that is, as SYSTEM (`resolvePredicateRelated` reads related values under system authority). It reads the folded parents' stored rows once, at most 500 ids per read. It resolves the plan's permission map once over those rows, with the SYSTEM context's own permission resolution, and likewise its one-hop related rows and its option labels; none of these moves while the update is judged. The plan is the parent's stored computed fields and formulas that read a folded roll-up, closed transitively (`storedExpressionsReading`). Each overlay then computes them in two passes, as one by one computes them:
  1. The stored computed fields, as the recompute's write computes them: over the write's image, the stored row with the folded roll-ups and no formula fields. A stored field that reads a formula therefore computes `null` here, as it does on every write. This pass uses the DECLARED option labels.
  2. The formulas, as the next read computes them: over that row, with the option labels the SYSTEM read uses.
  Both passes use the read path's own `applyFormulaPlan`. An object whose calculated fields read no folded roll-up reads nothing more. Validation still runs on every row before the one write: all-or-nothing is unchanged.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts` and `engine.ts` — `summaryDescriptorsReadByRules(childObject)`: the child's roll-up descriptors that some rule reads, from the cached #34439 analysis (`summaryFieldsReadByRules`, classes (i) and (ii)). It is wired through the facet host like `summaryForeignKeyColumns`. Added to the claim's file surface by the area (comment 6938143680 on #34465).
- `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` — one paragraph after the bulk-update one: a predicate update equals one-by-one updates, with its limits.
- `.changeset/34465-predicate-update-parent-summary-rule.md` — `patch` on `@objectstack/objectql`, BREAKING, FROM → TO and the one-line fix, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

## Why

Ruling 6377847361 (C, 「批量等于逐条，并发不保证」, inserts) and ruling record 6928862195 (B, 「被规则读到的合计不延后」, updateMany). The record's out-of-card finding named this door: "No ruling covers it". The seat ruled it the third door of the same family, route A, on the card (6938087434). The SQL stays in the database (one grouped aggregate per summary read), the hook and event shapes do not move (route B would have split the write into N by-id updates), and no function is left with a partial answer (route C).

What narrows, named in the changeset: a predicate update that one-by-one updates would refuse a row of is now refused, with `VALIDATION_FAILED` / 400, and writes nothing. Not moved: a rule that reads no summary, a predicate update matching one row, a by-id update, hooks and flow steps (they read the value from before the update, as ruling record 6928862195 states), and a rule of the parent itself (class (iii): it judges the summary once, after the write; outside this card, as the card's options analysis says).

## Tests

- `packages/objectql/src/summary-rollup.test.ts` — a new top-level `describe` (#34465) on the file's memory driver, where the roll-up recompute runs for real. A child carries five roll-ups that rules read (a filtered `count`, a `count`, `sum`, `min`, `avg`). Its class (i) rules read them one hop, and its class (ii) `requiredWhen: 'parent.line_count >= 3'` reads one on the header.
  - The one-by-one reference answer.
  - A predicate update refused as one by one refuses its second row (`VALIDATION_FAILED` / 400, nothing written) for the filtered `count`, `sum`, `avg` (a row outside the match included) and `min` (a matched row holding the extreme takes it with it).
  - A reparent: three lines moving under a header of one land under 1, 2, then 3, and the third needs `note`. A reparent under the line: all admitted.
  - A predicate update matching one row reads the stored value.
  - A rule reading a FORMULA (`remaining`) and one reading a STORED computed field (`headroom`) calculated from the `total` roll-up: the one-by-one reference, the predicate update refusing the second row, and under the line admitted.
  - The other direction: a row main refused (it read the stored total, 120) is admitted, because the row before it lowers the total to 70, as one by one admits it.
  - S2, each with its one-by-one reference: a formula reading a lookup hop and the roll-up (`cap_left = record.cap_ref.amount - record.total`), updated by a caller who cannot read the lookup's object (a read-scoping middleware): one by one refuses the second update, and a predicate update by the same caller is refused the same way, because the calculated field is computed under SYSTEM. A stored computed field reading a formula (`slack = record.remaining`): measured one by one it stays `null` on every write, because a write's image carries no formula, so the rule admits both rows, and the predicate update admits both.
  - CONTROL: an object whose rule reads no roll-up makes no aggregate read before its write, and admits as before.
  - The subject reads one grouped aggregate per roll-up a rule reads, before the write.
  - The file's fake driver learned `$null`: the engine widens a `$nin` to `$or [x $null, x $nin]`, and the fake answered `true` for any unknown operator.
- `packages/objectql/src/summary-batch-accumulation.test.ts` covers the fold and the loader on their own: count/sum/avg over a base holding the matched rows, min/max over a base leaving them out, reparent and header, the three left-out cases, and the statements the loader sends. It also checks that the fold hands the folded values to the dependents hook and patches only the calculated fields the row carries.

Ablation (`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, one mutation, taken on the fix commit before the branch was restarted on `main`, so the blobs below are that commit's `engine-update.ts`): the `summaryFold?.advance(i);` line in the `engine-update.ts` validation loop was deleted (anchor x1 → x0, blob `72635fb6ff22` → `79e693a8edb8`). Every row then reads the base as stored. The suites import the engine from source, so no rebuild was needed. Result: `Tests 5 failed | 97 passed (102)`.
- Red, as predicted: the filtered `count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min` and the reparent refusal.
- Green, as predicted: one-by-one, single match, under the line, CONTROL, bases-read, and every unit pin.
- Restore: blob `72635fb6ff22` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

Second ablation, for the calculated fields (at `06427b07`): `const computed = dependents?.(object, parentId, moved);` was replaced with `const computed = undefined as …;` (anchor x1 → x0, blob `2e7d129120ed` → `7e274c71df8f`). Result: `Tests 3 failed | 105 passed (108)`.
- Red, as predicted: the dependents unit pin, and the FORMULA and STORED computed refusals.
- Green, as predicted: the one-by-one formula reference, under the line, the other direction, and every earlier pin.
- Restore: blob `2e7d129120ed` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

Third and fourth ablations, for S2 (at `a7affccc`), one mutation each, `Tests 1 failed | 111 passed (112)` each, restored blob == HEAD:
- `resolveFormulaRelated(…, systemCtx)` → `(…, context)`: red is the caller/lookup refusal only.
- The line removing the formula fields from the write's image deleted: red is the stored-reads-formula pin only.

On the order of the two passes: L2's S2 asked for a stored field to compute after the formula it reads. That would compute a value one by one never stores: the reference pin measures a stored computed field reading a formula as `null` after every by-id write. So the stored pass runs first, over the image without formulas, as the write does, and the formulas after, as the read does; the fourth ablation reds that pin.

## Where "exact" is not reached (the three stored-value exceptions)

Route A (seat ruling on the card, 6938087434) asks each matched row to read the roll-up exactly as consecutive by-id updates would. In three cases the fold cannot say that value exactly. The roll-up then keeps reading the stored value, the value every row read before this change, rather than a guessed one. This applies to that roll-up for EVERY parent the update reads it for, not only the parent whose row or base caused it, because the case is decided once per roll-up per update. Every other roll-up a rule reads, and every parent field calculated from one, is still folded. A rule reading a dropped roll-up answers as it did before this PR, so nothing here can admit a row that main refuses.

1. **A summary `filter` that names a dotted path** (`{ 'account.kind': 'x' }`), **or one the in-memory filter walker refuses**. Whether a matched row counts depends on a field of ANOTHER record, reached through a reference. The matched row in memory carries the foreign key but not that record, so the in-memory walker cannot tell whether the row's old or new state passes the filter. The same limit applies on the insert arm (#25579). A filter the walker refuses (an operator it does not evaluate) cannot be judged in memory either, so it falls back the same way. Exact would need one extra read per hop, per row.
2. **A value that is not a finite number, in any matched row or any parent's base.** This covers a `sum` / `min` / `max` / `avg` over a date, a text, or a decimal that the driver returns as a string, either in a matched row or in the base the database answers. Folding needs arithmetic and ordering on the values. Comparing a JS string with a database decimal or date would invent an order that the database does not use. The same limit applies on the insert arm.
3. **A `min` / `max` when any one parent holds more than 5,000 matched rows** (`MIN_MAX_EXCLUDED_ID_BUDGET`). An extreme cannot be taken back out of an aggregate. So the base for `min` / `max` leaves the matched rows out with `id $nin (…)`. Parents are packed so that one statement names at most 500 parent ids and 5,000 excluded ids, far below SQLite's 32,766 and PostgreSQL's 65,535 bound parameters. One parent whose own matched set is larger than that cannot be excluded in one statement. `count` / `sum` / `avg` have no such limit: their base holds the matched rows as stored, and the fold subtracts each row's old part in memory, so no id list is sent.

Pinned: cases 1 and 3, and case 2 for a base that is not a number, in `summary-batch-accumulation.test.ts` (`loadPredicateUpdateSummaryBases`: a roll-up is left out). Case 2 for a matched value that is not a number is pinned in the same file (`createPredicateUpdateSummaryFold`: no fold). The user-facing docs state all three (`content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`), and so does the changeset.

## Acceptance notes

- Restarted from `main` after #34612 merged (b91cefa9). `origin/main` was merged again before the first runs (13741cb9), and again for the L2 delta (f63c9e3e). Both merges were clean.
- L2 delta (review 6943284591): S1, a rule reading a parent field calculated from a roll-up, is now folded (see What changes and the second ablation). N1, the direction a predicate update can move each way, and N2, which roll-ups and parents fall back to the stored value, are written into the changeset, the docs and the exceptions section.
- PR #34565 (#33876, same area) also edited `engine.ts`. It merged at 10:36Z as `6091b645`, after this head's last `main` merge. `git merge-tree --write-tree` of this head against `origin/main` with it (`48a6c3e4`) is clean.
- Cost: an object with no rule reading a roll-up of it, or an update matching one row, reads nothing more (pinned by CONTROL). Otherwise: one grouped aggregate per roll-up read, per 500 parents (for `min` / `max`, also per 5,000 excluded ids), before the write.
- Class (iii) (a rule of the parent itself judging the recompute's write) and the `readonlyWhen` bulk strip are outside this card, as the card's options analysis says.
- Follow-up #34821 (Blocked-by #34465): L2 nits N3 (row 0 reads the base even when the patch moves no roll-up) and N4 (no trace of the three fallbacks), and the same shape as S1 on the multi-row insert side (#34612's accumulator overlays the summary field only, so a rule reading a formula built on it still reads the stored value).
